sentences.show: In 1940, one man got himself arrested, so the Germans would send him to Auschwitz.
His name was Witold Pilecki, a Polish cavalry officer in the resistance.
Nobody knew what was really happening inside the new camp. A volunteer was needed. He said yes.
He let the Germans catch him in Warsaw, under a false name.
Days later, he was prisoner number 4859.
He survived slave labour and pneumonia. And he built a secret army, in cells of five.
His men smuggled out reports of the killings. They even built a radio, from smuggled parts.
His reports became a main source on Auschwitz for the Allies.
He hoped for an attack to free the camp. It never came.
So in April 1943, after two and a half years inside, he broke out through a bakery door.
Shot at and wounded, he made it back to the resistance.
A year later, he fought in the Warsaw Uprising.
After the war, Poland fell under communist rule. Pilecki stayed, and kept reporting to the government in exile.
In 1947, the secret police caught him. They tortured him. He gave up no one.
After a show trial, he was shot in the back of the head. His grave has never been found.
He walked into Auschwitz by choice, and came out alive. It was his own country that killed him.
For decades, they tried to erase his name. Subscribe, and help us say it.
